title: Arcanea: The Sovereign Depths
subtitle: Ancient power. Living worlds. Consequences that remain.
description: Twenty-four proposed boss encounters across twelve materially distinct dungeons, authored for adult cinematic fantasy, interconnected novels and readable encounter design. This is a staged creative collection, not an assertion of implemented playable game systems.

source.commitPurpose: Pinned canon baseline; all collection records are new local proposals.

bosses.name: Vorrak
bosses.title: The Cinder Maw
bosses.summary: A burrowing predator whose grinding jaws can turn a furnace wall into nesting gravel. Its threat comes from mass, heat and territorial certainty.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated fauna; expedition name recorded by the Cinder Mutual.
bosses.ecology: Consumes mineral grazers and iron-rich deposits around stable heat. Its six legs distribute weight on fractured crust; the forelimbs excavate while the middle pair brace. It follows sustained ground vibration, not supernatural knowledge of the player.
bosses.history: The cooling breach opened a warm nursery basin. Evacuated workers once diverted their hammer shifts away from it; Ithraden has deliberately restarted the loudest presses to drive Vorrak towards intruders.
bosses.rivalry: Ithraden steals the heat Vorrak needs and exploits its territorial charges. Open shutters expose the duelist but provoke the animal; rerouting the bypass separates their incentives.
bosses.movement: Slow lateral weight transfer precedes a committed forward shove. It can pivot only after lifting a middle brace leg, exposing a narrow safe crossing behind the shoulder.
bosses.entrance: A whole slab of the trench floor rises. The grinder jaw emerges first, pushing a dead press aside before the six legs unfold beneath it.

encounter.objective: Transfer the excavation route out of the nursery; drive Vorrak back or kill it, with visibly different ecological consequences.
encounter.arena: An annular trench with four solid basalt islands, weak crust between them and a controllable cooling bypass.

phases.name: Sounding
phases.trigger: First sustained vibration inside its nesting radius.
phases.action: It drums with a front leg; pebbles jump in the lane of an incoming jaw shove.
phases.counterplay: Leave the aligned lane and cross behind the shoulder during the middle-leg reset.

phases.name: Hot ground
phases.trigger: The bypass is opened or two nursery barriers are destroyed.
phases.action: It vents hot breath into a trench, then forces rubble into the resulting steam corridor.
phases.counterplay: Read the jaw’s dull internal heat, climb a solid island and reopen a clear return lane before steam builds.

phases.name: Return path
phases.trigger: A quiet warm route to the nursery is restored.
phases.action: It tests the route with alternating forefeet, then retreats unless attacked or followed.
phases.counterplay: Stop heavy movement, withdraw from the nursery mouth and let its full body clear before restoring the elevator.

encounter.failure: A collapsed crust traps equipment and forces retreat to an upper chain. Destroying the nursery triggers a persistent lethal defence rather than a scripted forgiving reset.
encounter.aftermath: A redirected Vorrak keeps the lower trench inhabited. Killing it opens a faster mining route but removes a major grazer control and changes the later expedition return.

bosses.anatomy: Huge six-legged basalt-skinned burrowing predator; broad wedge skull; interlocking mineral grinding lower-jaw plates; load-bearing keratin shoulder ridge; tiny recessed eyes.
bosses.materials: Rough living skin, iron-rich keratin, old pale pressure scars, dull heat inside the jaw only.

story.role: The first practical test of Tamsin Reed’s promise that the harbour can be rebuilt without repeating its wartime extraction.

bosses.name: Ithraden
bosses.title: The Furnace Exile
bosses.summary: A furnace tactician who chooses which parts of the arena are survivable. His forged shield arm is a working tool, and he uses it with the intimacy of a veteran operator.
bosses.faction: Void Ascendants, furnace occupation detachment.
bosses.ecology: Needs cooling water, replaceable arm liners and ore shipments. Disabling supply makes him less mobile between heat lanes but never magically deletes his combat skill.
bosses.history: Ithraden survived the foundry evacuation and later sold its bypass plans to the occupiers. His exile is a local sentence for that betrayal; no hidden divine pedigree excuses it.
bosses.rivalry: He keeps Vorrak agitated as an unwitting perimeter defence, yet fears the animal will break the shutter ring he needs.
bosses.movement: Short diagonal steps keep his shield facing heat. His blade controls one narrow lane while the forged forearm braces a shutter; he cannot defend both sides while operating it.
bosses.entrance: Behind a furnace wheel, an ordinary human hand wipes soot from a sight slit. The shutter opens, and he advances inside the only band of air cool enough to breathe.

encounter.objective: Stop the siege-alloy shipment and seize or disable the furnace controls.
encounter.arena: Four radial heat lanes separated by masonry wedges; the bypass handwheel sits opposite his initial position.

phases.name: Operating distance
phases.trigger: The challenger enters the control ring.
phases.action: A three-blow blade sequence ends with a shield shove towards a shutter; a visible handwheel movement precedes each heat lane.
phases.counterplay: Dodge across his blade side after the second blow, then punish the planted shield without entering the announced lane.

phases.name: Bleed pressure
phases.trigger: The bypass reduces furnace pressure.
phases.action: He removes an overheated liner and uses it as a short-lived burning barrier, making the shield arm slower until recooled.
phases.counterplay: Let the liner fall, circle through the cooled wedge and interrupt his approach to the water trough.

phases.name: Last shipment
phases.trigger: The lift is seized or the shipment brake is cut.
phases.action: He abandons static control and pursues the lift with direct sword attacks.
phases.counterplay: Use the exposed lift brake to choose the final fighting level; defeat, capture or force him away before the load departs.

encounter.failure: The shipment escapes on a visible lift countdown, supplying Rhaum’s later position. The party can survive and continue with that harder strategic state.
encounter.aftermath: A captured Ithraden is a prisoner with useful knowledge, not automatically redeemed. The furnace can reopen at reduced output under the workers’ own terms.

bosses.anatomy: Lean mature male human duelist with close-cropped grey hair, severe visible face, one forged right forearm ending in a broad functional heat shield, long ordinary left-hand blade, soot-worn leather and asymmetric heatproof cloth.
bosses.materials: Oxidized iron, heat-bleached leather, thick woven cloth, living human skin.

story.role: A chosen betrayer whose practical competence tempts Garrick Moss to accept an efficient but ruinous bargain.

bosses.name: Serath
bosses.title: The Reef Ascendant
bosses.summary: A thirty-metre hunter whose eight ribbon fins turn a drowned fort into an active feeding current. Beauty and danger are the same physical event.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated pelagic fauna.
bosses.ecology: Feeds on dense schools concentrated by reef flow. Cartilage and four fin pairs support slow station-keeping and abrupt lateral turns; it cannot follow divers through narrow stone passages.
bosses.history: Serath occupied the gulf after the reef matured. The garrison standard now starves the feeding corridor, pushing it into shallower passages where divers work.
bosses.rivalry: Morvane’s standard constricts its food supply. Serath attacks the standard’s moving cloth during current reversals and can accidentally break cover the divers depend on.
bosses.movement: Broad turns originate in the second fin pair. A folded ventral mouth signals a pass; a widening mouth and inward curl of the rear fins signal a suction strike.
bosses.entrance: A school of fish compresses into a silver wall. That wall parts along a curved seam, revealing nacre ribs beneath the passing hunter.

encounter.objective: Reopen the feeding current and survive the hunter’s territorial passes; killing remains possible at major cost to the reef system.
encounter.arena: A central gulf bordered by three air bells and stone channels too narrow for its body, with a sediment-choked living inlet valve.

phases.name: Closed current
phases.trigger: Divers enter the gulf while the inlet is blocked.
phases.action: Serath circles once, then draws loose debris towards its opening mouth.
phases.counterplay: Anchor behind a stone rib when debris starts moving; cross after the mouth closes and the tail clears.

phases.name: Turn of water
phases.trigger: The first sediment obstruction is cleared.
phases.action: The changed current pulls Serath laterally; its inner fins rake the near wall while the opposite flank opens.
phases.counterplay: Read which fin pair flares, use the outer current and work the next obstruction during its wide recovery turn.

phases.name: Feeding passage
phases.trigger: The inlet is fully restored.
phases.action: A shoal enters and Serath commits to a long upstream feeding run.
phases.counterplay: Clear the gulf and remove hanging lines from its route; follow in its wake only after displaced debris settles.

encounter.failure: An unanchored diver is swept to the lower recovery pocket with damaged air gear. Continued obstruction drives the hunter into the shallow route, closing a return path.
encounter.aftermath: A living Serath becomes a known seasonal hazard, not a mount. Successful divers chart its feeding interval for later civilian passage.

bosses.anatomy: Thirty-metre pelagic predator with a narrow sculpted head, broad ventral mouth and eight long ribbon fins arranged in four pairs; translucent nacre cartilage visible through thick blue-green skin; no humanoid eyes or dragon horns.
bosses.materials: Wet living skin, nacre cartilage, restrained violet sensory pores and clear trailing membrane edges.

story.role: Forces Brigid Vale to distinguish a navigable danger from an enemy that must be eliminated.

bosses.name: Morvane
bosses.title: The Drowned Standard
bosses.summary: A drowned standard-bearer still enforcing the occupation line across a reef that outlived his state.
bosses.faction: Voidtouched remnant of a drowned occupying force.
bosses.ecology: Bound to the physical standard and the garrison’s surviving command marks. Cannot leave the fortified reef or hear orders from an imagined opened prison.
bosses.history: Morvane held the bridge during a refused evacuation. The standard’s residual Shadow corruption preserves a narrow occupation programme, not a faithful personality reconstructed from the dead.
bosses.rivalry: Serath’s strikes damage his perimeter; he responds by tightening the standard’s anchoring lines and worsening the reef’s starvation.
bosses.movement: Pavise-first lateral shuffles resist current. Every hooked sweep requires the standard to leave its socket, briefly releasing tension in one inlet line.
bosses.entrance: A bronze faceplate turns beneath hanging cloth. The submerged bridge is suddenly cleared of drifting silt by a shield planted against the current.

encounter.objective: Remove the occupation standard from the inlet and preserve enough of the bridge for evacuation.
encounter.arena: A submerged bridge with three anchor sockets, a low side channel and two air pockets outside the standard’s sweep.

phases.name: The line holds
phases.trigger: A diver crosses the first command mark.
phases.action: He sweeps the hooked standard at waist height, then thrusts behind the shield; cloth tension indicates the sweep direction.
phases.counterplay: Drop into the side channel during the sweep and strike or release the temporarily slack anchor.

phases.name: Broken socket
phases.trigger: One anchor is released.
phases.action: He drags the pavise to the next socket and pulls a current-driven overhead strike.
phases.counterplay: Watch the standard cloth lift, stay close to the shield’s rear edge and remove the second anchoring pin during the long recovery.

phases.name: No shore to hold
phases.trigger: All anchor sockets are released.
phases.action: The standard loses its fixed sweep and Morvane advances with short heavy thrusts.
phases.counterplay: Lure him clear of the civilians’ bridge, separate him from the fallen standard and disable or contain the residual binding.

encounter.failure: Breaking the bridge isolates an air bell and changes the rescue route. A drowned or exhausted diver is recoverable only while a companion retains an anchored line.
encounter.aftermath: The standard can be secured as dangerous evidence in a sealed transport case. The reef current returns without implying that all Shadow in the world has been cleansed.

bosses.anatomy: Tall drowned revenant soldier with an enclosed salt-pitted bronze faceplate, waterlogged dark cloth, a broad cracked stone pavise and a long hooked military standard; no tentacles or coral crown.
bosses.materials: Salt deposits, heavy soaked cloth, pitted bronze, chipped basalt; restrained Shadow leakage beneath faceplate.

story.role: A material record of occupation whose defeat gives the divers proof of a suppressed evacuation order.

bosses.name: The Marrow Regent
bosses.title: Sovereign of the Empty Choir
bosses.summary: A resonating burial-ground predator with an ivory bill and six external rib struts. Its call becomes architecture when the bells answer.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated mutated fauna exploited by a Void Ascendant sect.
bosses.ecology: Uses low-frequency vibration to disturb burrowing prey, with range amplified by the burial bells. It is not omniscient; textile baffles and disconnected braces limit propagation.
bosses.history: The Regent nested in warm ceramic chambers before Vaust arrived. Repeated forced amplification has thickened its resonator tissue and made distant knocks trigger defensive displays.
bosses.rivalry: Vaust harvests its tissue and induces calls from the far tuning frame. The animal will pursue him when that stimulus is physically isolated and exposed.
bosses.movement: Long deliberate steps keep the torso stable. Before a sonic pulse, the six rib struts spread sequentially and the throat membrane changes from dull plum to stretched pale.
bosses.entrance: Dust rises from the floor before any body appears. A smooth bill enters one end of a burial bell and the folding mantle fills its mouth.

encounter.objective: Reach the tuning frame by disabling the forced amplification; redirect or defeat the Regent without destroying the whole burial avenue.
encounter.arena: Three connected bell chambers with movable felt baffles, low side tunnels and visible cedar resonance braces.

phases.name: Listening
phases.trigger: A loud impact travels along a connected brace.
phases.action: The Regent turns its bill towards the source and sends a cone pulse; hanging dust reveals the cone before the main pressure wave.
phases.counterplay: Break line of propagation behind a baffle or move into the next bell through the low side tunnel.

phases.name: Full mantle
phases.trigger: Vaust’s frame forces a second amplification.
phases.action: All six ribs unfold for a broad chamber pulse, followed by a vulnerable closed-mantle recovery.
phases.counterplay: Release a marked brace or brace behind the grounded baffle; cross the chamber while the mantle folds.

phases.name: Uncommanded animal
phases.trigger: The frame’s living resonator is disconnected.
phases.action: It follows the last loud stimulus instead of the artificial signal.
phases.counterplay: Create a deliberate sound route away from custodians, then keep the evacuation corridor quiet.

encounter.failure: Repeated bell destruction erases inscriptions and sends the animal towards the occupied annex. Custodian rescue becomes a separate timed consequence.
encounter.aftermath: A redirected animal retains a nesting chamber beyond a damped barrier. The name Regent remains an expedition epithet; no throne or cosmic station is established.

bosses.anatomy: Huge flightless birdlike predator with an elongated smooth ivory bill and a high narrow torso; six curved external rib struts form a folding resonator mantle, muscular dark featherless legs; no humanoid skull, antlers or crown.
bosses.materials: Aged ivory keratin, taut charcoal skin, chalk dust, dull plum throat membrane.

story.role: Makes Sabine Rook choose which evidence can be carried and which must be protected in place.

bosses.name: Vaust
bosses.title: The Bell Surgeon
bosses.summary: A calm acoustician who treats the burial avenue as a weapon he can finish while fighting you.
bosses.faction: Void Ascendants, escarpment acoustic cell.
bosses.ecology: A mortal operator dependent on intact bells, measured sightlines and a harvested resonator. His advantage is prepared transmission paths rather than unbounded voice magic.
bosses.history: Vaust adapted civilian surveying methods for siege range-finding. He chose the burial avenue because its custodians could not move their records quickly enough to resist occupation.
bosses.rivalry: He needs the Regent alive but tractable. The animal’s independent movement continually disrupts his calibration, giving an observant challenger opportunities he cannot entirely control.
bosses.movement: Economical sideways steps place a bell between him and an attacker. He commits both hands to each long tuning stroke and uses the hammer’s hooked heel for close defence.
bosses.entrance: Three gentle hammer taps arrive from different chambers. At the far frame, Vaust adjusts an ear guard and writes down how long your footsteps took to answer.

encounter.objective: Prevent the calibrated pulse from reaching the occupied annex and capture or destroy the firing method.
encounter.arena: A tuning platform overlooking the bell avenue, three transmission braces and a hanging resonator frame.

phases.name: Calibration
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches the final bell.
phases.action: He taps a brace, waits for its return and strikes the hammer where the echo predicts movement.
phases.counterplay: Change elevation after the first tap; the returning dust line marks the attack path.

phases.name: Live measurement
phases.trigger: Two braces are damped or severed.
phases.action: He moves the resonator to a surviving line and sweeps a wire frame at close range to force distance.
phases.counterplay: Close during the transfer, attack the support hand or pin the frame without standing in its line.

phases.name: Premature discharge
phases.trigger: The annex firing path is interrupted.
phases.action: He attempts a direct overload that will shatter the nearest bell and cover his retreat.
phases.counterplay: Read the rapid, irregular tapping; release the frame counterweight or force him off the grounded firing plate before the final strike.

encounter.failure: An undamped path carries a destructive pulse into the annex, injuring custodians and destroying specific records. This loss persists even if Vaust is killed afterwards.
encounter.aftermath: Surviving plans can establish how the acoustic cell supports the exterior siege. A living Vaust remains an accountable enemy with his own strategy.

bosses.anatomy: Compact older male human with bald scarred head and measured expression; fitted dark work coat and ceramic ear guards; holds a long tuning hammer and a wire-framed cracked resonator; no medical gore.
bosses.materials: Chipped ceramic, worn steel, waxed linen, ordinary mature skin.

story.role: An antagonist who destroys evidence for military advantage, establishing the trilogy’s conflict over what can be proved.

bosses.name: Orryx
bosses.title: The Briar Cataphract
bosses.summary: An armoured canopy hunter that can climb the structures its opponents mistake for safety.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated forest arthropod.
bosses.ecology: Territorial near its molting shelf and clutch. Four locomotor legs carry the thorax; two raised blade forelimbs hook prey and terrain. It senses transmitted vibration better than motion through open air.
bosses.history: The old aqueduct offers reliable drumming surfaces above a flooded ravine. Survey traffic has concentrated during its breeding season, creating a conflict that did not exist at lower footfall.
bosses.rivalry: Serevra uses its territorial boundaries to protect her platform, but refuses to destroy its clutch because doing so would drive it through both expeditions’ camps.
bosses.movement: Stops completely before a two-stage hook and pull. After climbing, its rear legs must find purchase before the blade limbs can strike again.
bosses.entrance: A blade limb hooks over an aqueduct edge. Roots snap one at a time as the narrow thorax rises into the morning light.

encounter.objective: Open a supply crossing by rerouting vibration or defeating the animal; keep the nesting shelf separate from the crossing objective.
encounter.arena: Two aqueduct spans, a hanging root bridge and a white watch pier, with water sluices that can mask or redirect sound.

phases.name: Claimed span
phases.trigger: A heavy footstep reaches its nearest pier.
phases.action: It hooks the span, then pulls its head into a forward snapping strike; the hook remains visible before the pull.
phases.counterplay: Leave the hooked edge, cross behind its raised limb and attack only during the rear-leg purchase pause.

phases.name: High approach
phases.trigger: The direct span is flooded or its first perch fails.
phases.action: It climbs through roots and drops a blade across the next landing.
phases.counterplay: Watch root tension and falling moss; stay on an unconnected rope line or move to a pier outside that root network.

phases.name: Crossing window
phases.trigger: The old water channel is reopened.
phases.action: Water masks the supply party while Orryx turns towards a prepared drumming lure.
phases.counterplay: Stop using the resonant stone route and escort the convoy across the quieter root bridge before the lure breaks.

encounter.failure: A severed root bridge isolates supplies. Killing the clutch makes Orryx abandon predictable defence for a pursuit through the camps.
encounter.aftermath: The reopened channel supports future seasonal crossings; the field guide records a closure during the next molt instead of declaring the forest conquered.

bosses.anatomy: Massive six-legged forest arthropod with a low forward-armoured head, tall segmented thorax and two long folded blade forelimbs held above four locomotor legs; thornlike growth only along chitin joints, no mammal eyes.
bosses.materials: Matte dark olive chitin, reddish joint membranes, wet moss caught in grooves.

story.role: Introduces Corvin Holt’s conflict between a survey deadline and the living conditions a map must describe.

bosses.name: Serevra
bosses.title: The Pale Huntress
bosses.summary: A formidable ranger whose claim is practical and limited: she built a rescue route, and she will not let a better-funded expedition take it by force.
bosses.faction: Independent Pale Line expedition; proposed Gate-Touched mortal.
bosses.ecology: Needs dry bowstrings, recovered arrows and concealed rope exits. Wind and water affect her range; neither pale camouflage nor Gate training makes her invisible.
bosses.history: Serevra lost her original route to a ravine collapse, rebuilt the aqueduct approach and rescued two stranded surveyors. Her contract now gives her crew a legitimate access claim contested by the Meridian Survey.
bosses.rivalry: She understands Orryx’s nesting radius but cannot command it. Using the animal as a weapon risks the rescue route that gives her claim its moral and contractual weight.
bosses.movement: A single planted draw alternates with rapid lateral relocation along prepared ropes. Her release shoulder and bow cant disclose whether the next shot pins cover or targets movement.
bosses.entrance: An arrow cuts the loose end of a rope beside your hand. She stands on the distant white pier, gives her name and states the boundary once.

encounter.objective: Win passage through a declared contest, negotiate shared access or survive a hostile crossing; surrender remains a valid outcome.
encounter.arena: Three sighted piers and two rope exits with a clearly marked noncombat shelter for both crews.

phases.name: Declared measure
phases.trigger: A challenger accepts the crossing contest or breaches the boundary.
phases.action: She fires a visible ranging arrow, then attempts a pinning shot at the route it marks.
phases.counterplay: Change routes after the ranging shot, use stone cover and close only when her bow arm is extended.

phases.name: Broken sightline
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches the second pier.
phases.action: She releases a prepared rope and descends to a lower firing shelf.
phases.counterplay: Watch the escape knot move; secure the upper rope or use water spray to reveal the new angle.

phases.name: Within reach
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches her platform or meets the agreed score.
phases.action: She transitions to short bow strikes and a draw held at close range, then acknowledges a clean disarm or boundary loss.
phases.counterplay: Do not attack the noncombat shelter; use a controlled disarm, accept mutual withdrawal or state the negotiated claim.

encounter.failure: Harming the shelter ends the legitimate contest and turns both crews against the challenger. Losing the contest costs access time rather than a mandatory death.
encounter.aftermath: A fair resolution makes Serevra a recurring competitor who can cooperate without becoming subordinate. A violent seizure creates a durable human rivalry.

bosses.anatomy: Adult human woman ranger with weathered brown skin, tightly bound black braids, pale ash camouflage cloak cut short at bow arm, long asymmetric recurved bow and simple bone range markers; believable athletic proportions.
bosses.materials: Tough barkcloth, hide, dark wood, worn steel, rain on skin.

story.role: A rival with reasons to win, forcing Corvin to earn a professional relationship rather than collect a follower.

bosses.name: The Sundered Engine
bosses.title: A Sun Without a Master
bosses.summary: A solar artillery construct whose obsolete map turns a functioning road into an enemy approach.
bosses.faction: Abandoned Forged military apparatus; no active allegiance.
bosses.ecology: Depends on direct sunlight, intact mirror facets and functional leg joints. Clouds reduce beam output but do not stop its physical bracing and shutter attacks.
bosses.history: The Engine survived the fortress’s last storm with one map plate and a damaged targeting linkage. It cannot distinguish the relocated civilian road from the former assault ramp.
bosses.rivalry: Rhaum wants its map plate replaced with his own firing plan. The Engine currently treats his ammunition lift as an unauthorised approach and destroys the supplies he needs.
bosses.movement: Two arms brace before the chest mirror rotates; the other pair move shutter plates. Its mass prevents an immediate reversal after it commits to a ramp.
bosses.entrance: A mirror shadow passes over the evacuation cistern. Above it, the construct plants all four arms and raises its chest towards the sun.

encounter.objective: Defocus the array or replace the obsolete road-denial instruction without letting Rhaum capture the targeting assembly.
encounter.arena: A stepped firing ring with three shadow pockets, two manual observation shutters and a reachable rear maintenance platform.

phases.name: Find the sun
phases.trigger: Direct sunlight reaches the chest mirror.
phases.action: A broad pale reflection narrows into a beam that sweeps one ramp.
phases.counterplay: Move during the broad reflection and stay inside a hard shadow; attack a brace joint after the sweep stops.

phases.name: Manual defence
phases.trigger: Two targeting shutters are jammed.
phases.action: It advances with heavy shutter-plate strikes and repositions to a new solar angle.
phases.counterplay: Read which brace arm lifts, cross beneath the opposite shutter and ride the maintenance lift while the legs reset.

phases.name: Defocus window
phases.trigger: The rear maintenance platform is reached.
phases.action: The chest mirror locks for recalibration, exposing the defocus linkage while a timed mechanical sweep clears the platform.
phases.counterplay: Anchor before the sweep, operate the linkage between passes and choose permanent defocus or a restricted civilian-safe map.

encounter.failure: A destroyed cistern exit forces the evacuation column onto the exposed road. Leaving the map plate intact for Rhaum strengthens his later artillery position.
encounter.aftermath: Permanent defocus leaves a heavy but non-artillery salvage machine. A revised map creates a limited guardian of the passage with explicit maintenance obligations.

bosses.anatomy: Twenty-metre four-armed military construct with a short broad torso, two massive load-bearing legs and a broken concave mirror embedded in its chest; one pair of arms braces, the other aims heavy shutter plates; no humanoid glowing face.
bosses.materials: Tarnished bronze, cut dark stone, real mirror facets, heavy joints and pale ceramic heat liners.

story.role: An encounter about operational responsibility whose consequences determine whether Tamsin’s supply route stays open.

bosses.name: Rhaum
bosses.title: The Last Artillerist
bosses.summary: A siege captain who can make one narrow ramp impossible to cross, until the logistics supporting him are broken.
bosses.faction: Void Ascendants, high citadel artillery detachment.
bosses.ecology: Carries limited charged ammunition and needs prepared recoil notches. His harness distributes load but cannot let him fire the heavy cannon accurately while running.
bosses.history: Rhaum commanded a failed valley siege and now seeks a weapon that will remove his dependence on ordinary crews. His fear of another defeat drives calculated expendability, not a secret wish to be saved.
bosses.rivalry: The Sundered Engine denies his supply lift. He alternates attempts to capture it with volleys that further damage the mirror he hopes to command.
bosses.movement: Moves slowly between pre-sighted buttresses, then locks the harness into a notch. A kneeling recoil stance and visible breech vent distinguish a full shot from a short suppressing discharge.
bosses.entrance: A cannon report arrives before the captain is visible. Stone chips fall from the only ramp wide enough for the waiting evacuation wagons.

encounter.objective: Break the artillery position and keep the civilian supply lift operational.
encounter.arena: A zigzag ramp with four firing notches, destructible upper parapets and an ammunition lift on a visible cycle.

phases.name: Range held
phases.trigger: The challenger leaves the cistern cover.
phases.action: He vents the breech, locks into a notch and fires a straight penetrating shot; the vent precedes the muzzle charge.
phases.counterplay: Move across the lane during venting and close under the notch’s minimum depression angle.

phases.name: Ammunition denied
phases.trigger: The supply lift is stopped or two ammunition crates are seized.
phases.action: He uses short suppressing blasts and shoves with the barrel while moving towards his reserve.
phases.counterplay: Force movement between notches, attack the exposed harness buckle and keep the reserve physically separated.

phases.name: Last charged round
phases.trigger: Only his visibly marked reserve round remains.
phases.action: He commits to a long charge aimed at the civilian lift brake.
phases.counterplay: Interrupt the planted stance, pull the lift behind the stone sill or redirect the shot by rotating the damaged recoil notch.

encounter.failure: The civilian lift brake breaks and the evacuation must use a slower route; surviving supplies determine how many loads can be recovered before night.
encounter.aftermath: Seized artillery records expose the timing of Draeven’s blockade. Rhaum’s capture or death changes military intelligence, not the world’s metaphysical order.

bosses.anatomy: Broad older human siege captain in a practical dark military coat, weathered metal shoulder brace, bare stern face, carrying a massive shoulder-mounted recoil-balanced arcane cannon supported by a belt harness; no full-body ornamental armour.
bosses.materials: Worn steel, soot, stiff wool, leather harness, faint energy deep inside breech.

story.role: Connects the furnace shipment to the harbour campaign and makes earlier resource choices alter a later encounter.

bosses.name: The Unfaced Pilgrim
bosses.title: Bearer of the Missing Step
bosses.summary: A traveller-shaped phenomenon that repeats a route one step out of agreement with its own shadow.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated bounded spatial manifestation; ontology unresolved.
bosses.ecology: Exists only inside the Lacuna chamber and responds to occupied stair positions. It does not hunt beyond the doorway or turn ordinary darkness into evil.
bosses.history: Three survey parties recorded the figure with different clothing details but the same displaced step. The collection preserves those reports as disputed observations rather than an omniscient origin story.
bosses.rivalry: Ultharen closes routes the Pilgrim has just crossed. Whether this is cooperation, maintenance or coincidental rule interaction remains unresolved; the observable timing is consistent.
bosses.movement: Moves at walking speed on marked steps. Its ceiling shadow commits one step ahead; it cannot change that announced destination during the same footfall.
bosses.entrance: A wet footprint appears on a dry ceiling stair. Below it, a tall cloth-folded figure descends into the place your next step would occupy.

encounter.objective: Recover the missing surveyor’s tether and establish a traversable return without assuming the manifestation must die.
encounter.arena: Five marked landings in one chamber, an ordinary doorway and a ceiling return visible from the central landing.

phases.name: One step early
phases.trigger: The entrant occupies the second marked landing.
phases.action: The ceiling shadow selects a destination; the figure then reaches across the corresponding real step.
phases.counterplay: Read the shadow’s foot before moving and choose the unoccupied adjacent landing.

phases.name: Crossed route
phases.trigger: A tether is attached to the blocked junction.
phases.action: The figure follows the tether’s sequence in reverse, closing distance on anyone who repeats their own path.
phases.counterplay: Use an unused side step, maintain the external anchor and let the announced route complete before doubling back.

phases.name: Ordinary rain
phases.trigger: The blocked tether is returned to the entrance line.
phases.action: It walks to the threshold and stops with one foot inside the chamber.
phases.counterplay: Carry the recovered surveyor out while preserving the external anchor; attacking at the threshold restarts its local sequence.

encounter.failure: A misread step returns the entrant to the previous landing and abrades the tether. Exhausting the tether leaves a harder recovery route, not an arbitrary cosmological punishment.
encounter.aftermath: The Pilgrim remains an observable unresolved presence. A successful chart records reliable behaviours and explicitly omits a claimed true origin.

bosses.anatomy: Very tall lean figure whose head is a folded hollow of matte ivory cloth rather than a face; long jointed hands visible, feet ordinary and grounded, severe charcoal travel layers, one plain stone staff.
bosses.materials: Matte cloth, dry stone, weathered bare hands; no black smoke cloud.

story.role: Tests Jolant Grey’s willingness to publish an incomplete but useful account.

bosses.name: Ultharen
bosses.title: The Folded Colossus
bosses.summary: A moving arrangement of immense arches that changes which parts of a stair are neighbours.
bosses.faction: Experimental bounded construct; maker unresolved.
bosses.ecology: Its hinges and stone supports require physical contact with the chamber. It cannot fold external mountains, create worlds or rewrite history.
bosses.history: Old abrasion marks imply configurations predating the road crews. Those marks support a history of movement, not a verified account of construction or intelligence.
bosses.rivalry: Its rotation follows the Pilgrim’s completed crossings by one interval. Stopping an arch interrupts that pattern but makes no claim about which entity has authority.
bosses.movement: Four blunt supports reposition before an arch turns. Dust sheds from the next active hinge, and the empty central volume remains a stable landmark during rotation.
bosses.entrance: The landing in front of you rises slowly. What seemed to be a doorway lifts on four supports, revealing another stair behind its empty centre.

encounter.objective: Lock a safe route long enough to extract trapped surveyors and their evidence.
encounter.arena: The same bounded Lacuna chamber, with three rotating arches, five marked landings and two accessible friction locks.

phases.name: New neighbours
phases.trigger: The first surveyor tether crosses its central arch.
phases.action: An arch turns ninety degrees, exchanging two connected landings; hinge dust announces the turning side.
phases.counterplay: Stand on a marked landing outside the hinge sweep and cross only after the stone contacts settle.

phases.name: Load rejection
phases.trigger: A friction lock is inserted.
phases.action: The construct raises one support and drops a short crushing load onto the blocked joint.
phases.counterplay: Leave the support’s shadow, brace the lock from the remote socket and use the unloaded arch to reach the second mechanism.

phases.name: Held configuration
phases.trigger: Both friction locks engage.
phases.action: The remaining free arch cycles slowly to shed excess load.
phases.counterplay: Time the extraction through its empty centre, remove nonessential weight and leave the locks engaged until the last tether clears.

encounter.failure: An overloaded lock breaks and rearranges the route while the people remain on marked landings. Recovery requires a longer physical circuit; no character vanishes by unexplained fiat.
encounter.aftermath: The chamber can be mapped in a documented held state. Long-term stability remains unproven and must not be advertised as a permanent portal network.

bosses.anatomy: Nonhumanoid walking architectural creature composed of three immense interlocking pale stone arches on four blunt jointed supports; an empty central volume, no face, no runes or orb core.
bosses.materials: Ancient limestone, black friction marks, dust shed from articulated contacts.

story.role: Turns a mystery into an engineering extraction without resolving its metaphysical origin.

bosses.name: Hroven
bosses.title: The Rimebound King
bosses.summary: A scarred mountain predator whose immense forequarters can break the floor it stands on.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated mountain fauna.
bosses.ecology: Uses a warm channel for winter shelter and hunts fish concentrated beneath thinning ice. Its forelimbs deliver weight-driven blows; its short hindquarters make steep retreat slower than a forward lunge.
bosses.history: Old restraint scars suggest a failed hauling programme recorded in monastery fragments. This history explains human caution but does not make the animal a moral victim who must forgive anyone.
bosses.rivalry: Kethrane’s warming route attracts it to the seed bridge. She can keep it away with noise only by risking the fragile vault floor.
bosses.movement: Shoulders rise before a forepaw slam, then body weight shifts across the ice. A low head and compressed hindquarters announce the shorter but faster lunge.
bosses.entrance: Fish scatter under a clear floor panel. A dark nose presses through the ice, followed by a forepaw wider than a person’s chest.

encounter.objective: Redirect Hroven towards an unoccupied warm outlet or defeat it while preserving the controlled seed-warming route.
encounter.arena: An ice nave with timber load mats, a visible thaw channel and two manually divertible warm outlets.

phases.name: Claimed warmth
phases.trigger: The party enters the occupied channel span.
phases.action: It strikes the floor with a raised forepaw, sending visible whitening cracks towards the nearest heavy footing.
phases.counterplay: Spread weight, move onto a timber mat and avoid the widening fracture rather than only the paw.

phases.name: Broken surface
phases.trigger: Two ice panels fail or a warm outlet is changed.
phases.action: It lunges between exposed water edges and uses the current to climb back onto ice.
phases.counterplay: Read its compressed hindquarters, sidestep onto anchored timber and open the unoccupied outlet during the climb.

phases.name: New shelter
phases.trigger: The alternate outlet warms sufficiently.
phases.action: It follows fish into the new channel, stopping to test any pursuit behind it.
phases.counterplay: Keep the bridge quiet and withdraw along the marked timber route; continued attacks convert the retreat into a final defensive fight.

encounter.failure: Heavy impacts collapse the warming antechamber, reducing the viable seed stock and forcing an immediate evacuation.
encounter.aftermath: A redirected animal occupies a separated outlet. The monastery can retain a limited cold store, with a documented closure zone rather than a tame guardian.

bosses.anatomy: Enormous pale mountain ursid with elongated powerful forequarters, short heavy hindquarters, narrow small-eyed head, ice-caked dark nose, long frost-matted guard hair and old iron restraint scars; no crown or jewellery.
bosses.materials: Coarse damp ivory fur, ice crystals, dark skin and breath vapour.

story.role: Makes Brigid’s salvage ambitions contend with the physical requirements of keeping living cargo alive.

bosses.name: Kethrane
bosses.title: The White Vigil
bosses.summary: A disciplined expedition protector who has already paid for the route another party intends to claim.
bosses.faction: Independent White Vigil expedition; Academy-trained mortal.
bosses.ecology: A human fighter constrained by footing, breath and the need to keep the seed bridge intact. Training enables deliberate control, not immunity to cold or steel.
bosses.history: Kethrane’s crew discovered the viable stock and spent weeks warming it. Their sponsor claims exclusive custody; she doubts that claim but will not abandon the people who made extraction possible.
bosses.rivalry: Hroven occupies the channel her crew needs. She can repel it but cannot both fight on the ice and regulate the vault temperature.
bosses.movement: Low lateral guards become sliding countersteps on prepared frost. Her leading heel sets before a committed cut; on bare timber she loses the long glide but gains a faster stop.
bosses.entrance: Beyond the thaw water, a woman scrapes ice from the edge of her blade and tells the approaching party exactly how many people are still behind her.

encounter.objective: Earn shared custody by a controlled duel or agreement while keeping both expedition crews and the viable stock safe.
encounter.arena: A narrow bridge with two timber passing platforms, a marked surrender recess and a fragile warming chamber below.

phases.name: The bridge is held
phases.trigger: An armed challenger crosses the agreed mark.
phases.action: She makes two measured lateral cuts, then a sliding counterstep that punishes an immediate chase.
phases.counterplay: Watch the leading heel, wait for the glide to end and use the passing platform to change the angle.

phases.name: Ground changed
phases.trigger: A timber mat is placed or ice is broken.
phases.action: She shortens her stance and switches to close binds and shoulder checks.
phases.counterplay: Use blade control and a clean disarm; do not retreat through the warming controls with a weapon raised.

phases.name: Custody decision
phases.trigger: A clean disarm, agreed touch score or mutual withdrawal occurs.
phases.action: She lowers the point but keeps her crew’s exit open while terms are stated.
phases.counterplay: Honor the surrender recess and commit to a verifiable division of transport, seed stock and labour.

encounter.failure: A strike into the warming machinery kills part of the stock and ends the controlled duel. Losing fairly costs priority and transport capacity rather than life.
encounter.aftermath: Kethrane can become a recurring equal whose support depends on honoured agreements. She retains her crew and the right to refuse later requests.

bosses.anatomy: Mature human warrior woman with shaved dark hair, damaged pale lamellar armour over heavy grey wool, exposed serious face, long two-handed straight blade with an ordinary dark hilt; one asymmetric ice-crusted shoulder cloak.
bosses.materials: Scratched steel, felted wool, frost, human weathered skin.

story.role: A sustained rivalry that makes cooperation an earned political achievement rather than a reward for violence.

bosses.name: The Verdigris Monarch
bosses.title: Heart of the Living Seam
bosses.summary: An immense root-and-mineral organism that holds a wet crater together by continuously moving through it.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated proposed harmonic mutation; no divine identity.
bosses.ecology: Transports mineral-rich water through root channels and sheds stone leaves that shelter smaller organisms. Its movement opens sinkholes while closing older ones; stability is dynamic, not a frozen ideal.
bosses.history: The living seam arose in altered crater soil and was later cultivated by researchers. The current organism exceeds their records. Its exact emergence remains a local research question, not a replacement for Arcanea’s creation history.
bosses.rivalry: Small Khaross colonies prune blocked channels; the present infestation strips live conduits faster than the Monarch can reroute them. Attacking all parasites indiscriminately can also block drainage.
bosses.movement: Root legs lift one at a time, leaving three supports. A brightening seam precedes a mineral extrusion; a dimming seam precedes subsidence.
bosses.entrance: The causeway descends without breaking. Across the crater, a root rises from beneath a laboratory and lifts a terrace into the sunlight.

encounter.objective: Stabilise an extraction route and reduce the destructive infestation without severing the living water network.
encounter.arena: Four terraced levels linked by causeways, active root conduits and visible breathing sinkholes.

phases.name: Displaced terrace
phases.trigger: The extraction crew cuts a living conduit.
phases.action: The Monarch lifts a root and the connected terrace begins to sink; light drains from the exposed seam first.
phases.counterplay: Leave the dimming route, move onto an independent stone footing and close the extraction valve.

phases.name: Crystal defence
phases.trigger: Live roots are repeatedly damaged or the parasite enters a main channel.
phases.action: A seam brightens before blunt mineral leaves extrude across a chosen route.
phases.counterplay: Read the bright channel, move across rather than along it and use dead mineral cover while clearing the parasite from the junction.

phases.name: New circulation
phases.trigger: Two main channels are cleared and extraction stops.
phases.action: Water returns along an altered route, lifting one terrace and draining another.
phases.counterplay: Reposition the transport line to the new stable causeway and allow the root leg to settle before loading it.

encounter.failure: Severing the main network drains the wet terraces and collapses the high-yield route. Killing the Monarch provides immediate ore at a lasting ecological and settlement cost.
encounter.aftermath: A stabilised crater supports limited dry-seam work and repeated observation. The creature stays wild and its growth continues beyond the expedition’s needs.

bosses.anatomy: Huge plant-mineral organism with a hollow cylindrical trunk torso and four thick root legs, a low asymmetric crown of broad stone leaves, no face or deer antlers; luminous jade channels only where bark has split.
bosses.materials: Rough bark, malachite-like living crystal, wet soil, stone leaf surfaces.

story.role: Forces Fenwick Darr to replace an extraction forecast with a binding lower-yield contract.

bosses.name: Khaross
bosses.title: The Gilded Parasite
bosses.summary: A mineral-feeding parasite whose beautiful shell records the channels it has stolen.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated local parasite; outbreak amplified by extraction.
bosses.ecology: Rasps living mineral conduits and stores conductive sap under metallic biological shell plates. Small populations clear blocked growth; the large individual thrives on newly cut surfaces and warm laboratory drains.
bosses.history: Old casings appear in the earliest research beds. The present outbreak follows recent trench cuts, making it a consequence of altered feeding access rather than a newly invented evil species.
bosses.rivalry: Feeds on the Monarch yet depends on its continued circulation. When a main root dies, Khaross abandons it and seeks the next live channel, exposing an exploitable migration route.
bosses.movement: A wave of short legs carries the long body around narrow roots. The head can reverse along its own track faster than the whole shell can turn.
bosses.entrance: A gold-coloured seam peels away from a root. Dozens of legs unfold underneath, and the stolen jade light continues moving inside the shell.

encounter.objective: Separate the outbreak individual from the main water network and contain or kill it without poisoning the crater.
encounter.arena: A ring of mineral roots around a dry laboratory terrace, with controllable warm drains and dead-channel traps.

phases.name: Rasping circuit
phases.trigger: The party approaches an occupied root junction.
phases.action: Its antennae touch a live seam before the head follows with a short rasping rush.
phases.counterplay: Watch the antenna contact, cross onto a dead stone surface and strike the exposed underside during the root transfer.

phases.name: Stolen charge
phases.trigger: Two shell conduits are damaged.
phases.action: Stored sap brightens under a segment before it is expelled in a narrow corrosive jet.
phases.counterplay: Move away from the bright segment’s vents, use the dry terrace’s stone lip and wait for that shell plate to empty.

phases.name: False feeding route
phases.trigger: A warm drain leads into the dead-channel trap.
phases.action: It leaves the main root and accelerates along the prepared path, reversing if the temperature drops.
phases.counterplay: Maintain the drain until the tail clears, close both isolation wedges and choose containment or a focused final fight on dead stone.

encounter.failure: Breaking a sap reservoir over a living junction kills that conduit and redirects the outbreak into another terrace.
encounter.aftermath: A contained individual enables controlled study; indiscriminate eradication is not framed as automatically beneficial. The visible outbreak and ordinary small colonies remain distinct.

bosses.anatomy: Long predatory centipede-like organism with thin hammered-gold-coloured natural shell plates and dark flexible belly, dozens of short functional legs, forked sensory antennae and a blunt rasping mouth; no human face.
bosses.materials: Matte metallic biological shell, black wet chitin, jade sap; gold is ecological colour not ornament.

story.role: Exposes the difference between a useful ecosystem role and an intolerable local population event.

bosses.name: Avarra
bosses.title: The Glass Sovereign
bosses.summary: A Celestial duelist who makes every inch of an almost empty court matter. Her authority is a proposed local appointment, not a new Gate.
bosses.faction: Court of the Unbroken Light; proposed Celestial presider.
bosses.ecology: Uses three substantial quartz blades whose paths remain visible. She redirects light within the court’s optical architecture; the blades retain weight, collision and recovery constraints.
bosses.history: Avarra accepted the court’s revised nonlethal charter and has honoured it despite petitions to restore blood judgement. The older Warden cannot interpret every revision, so her fidelity to the terms is tested by the machinery beside her.
bosses.rivalry: The Prism Warden sometimes marks a surrendered entrant as an unauthorised occupant. Avarra will interrupt her own advantage to uphold the stated charter, without automatically disabling a mechanism she cannot safely reach.
bosses.movement: Measured footwork assigns one blade to pressure, one to guard and one to recovery. A blade rotated edge-on briefly disappears against the light but its shadow and sound remain legible.
bosses.entrance: Three quartz blades descend separately to the court. Avarra follows at walking pace, reads the chosen terms aloud and leaves the first attack to the challenger.

encounter.objective: Win the declared passage trial by clean touches, boundary control or disarm; protect a surrendered entrant when the old protocol intervenes.
encounter.arena: An open duel court with quartz fins, a marked boundary, two surrender recesses and rotating spectator shutters.

phases.name: Three measures
phases.trigger: The challenger confirms the trial conditions.
phases.action: One blade advances, one guards her flank and one returns through a fixed recovery arc.
phases.counterplay: Track the returning blade rather than chasing the attacker; cross its completed arc to reach her open side.

phases.name: Light divided
phases.trigger: The challenger scores two clean measures or controls the central mark.
phases.action: She rotates a blade into a visible light band before a long lateral sweep.
phases.counterplay: Read the blade’s bright edge and floor shadow, pass under the near end or move beyond the marked terminating fin.

phases.name: Terms upheld
phases.trigger: The Warden flags a surrendering entrant.
phases.action: Avarra diverts a blade to protect the recess, leaving her own scoring defence incomplete.
phases.counterplay: Pause scoring to help contain the Warden, or finish the agreed measure without striking the protected entrant; the charter records the choice.

encounter.failure: Leaving the boundary concedes a measure. Attacking a surrender recess ends the trial and closes lawful passage until restitution is adjudicated.
encounter.aftermath: A victory grants passage under stated terms, not ownership of the court or Avarra’s service. The charter discrepancy becomes a repair obligation shared by the two valleys.

bosses.anatomy: 3.2-metre adult female celestial duelist with mature angular face, deep-set dark eyes, severe smoke-grey silk and white mineral chest mantle; three substantial floating smoky-quartz blades, no crown or wings.
bosses.materials: Natural mature skin, weighted silk, chipped translucent quartz, worn ivory stone.

story.role: Makes a fair victory more demanding than killing, and gives Brigid a lasting public obligation alongside the route she wins.

bosses.name: The Prism Warden
bosses.title: Measure of the Court
bosses.summary: An optical sentinel that can divide a beam accurately and apply an obsolete rule disastrously.
bosses.faction: Court of the Unbroken Light; bounded Forged apparatus.
bosses.ecology: Requires incident light and clear quartz paths. Mineral inclusions scatter energy, so each active beam has a visible source and ending; occlusion works physically.
bosses.history: Its defence programme predates the court’s latest surrender charter. Previous presiders added manual pauses instead of replacing its core measure, leaving a documented conflict between law and machinery.
bosses.rivalry: Avarra’s commitment to the revised charter interrupts its original programme. It treats her protective blade as an obstruction to route around, not as a divine enemy.
bosses.movement: Four tapered feet reposition around a rotating prism. Horizontal vanes align before a split beam; thick crystal limits the speed of a complete reversal.
bosses.entrance: A single ray enters an empty court. The sentinel turns once, and two narrow lines of light stop precisely at the feet of a surrendered petitioner.

encounter.objective: Place the sentinel into a verifiable maintenance hold and prevent it firing into a surrender recess.
encounter.arena: The trial court’s side lane, with three shutters, two ground sockets and one accessible mechanical pause linkage.

phases.name: Measure occupied
phases.trigger: An entrant remains in a surrender recess after the old countdown.
phases.action: The prism aligns, then divides one ray into two marked firing lanes.
phases.counterplay: Move a shutter to occlude the source and approach from the unlit side while the vanes remain aligned.

phases.name: Route around
phases.trigger: The first firing path is blocked.
phases.action: It steps to a second socket and sweeps a glass vane through the maintenance lane.
phases.counterplay: Watch the lifting foot, leave the vane’s horizontal plane and pin the vacated socket before it can return.

phases.name: Maintenance hold
phases.trigger: Both operating sockets are pinned.
phases.action: The prism slows but attempts one final alignment using diffuse storm light.
phases.counterplay: Close the remaining shutter and pull the mechanical pause linkage; verify that the vanes settle before entering the recess.

encounter.failure: A failed hold injures the protected petitioner and invalidates the active trial. Avarra survives as an independent witness who will report exactly what occurred.
encounter.aftermath: The apparatus remains paused until its rule set is reconciled with the charter. Restarting it without that change is explicitly not a successful restoration.

bosses.anatomy: Tall narrow four-legged crystalline sentinel with a single vertical rotating prism torso, tapered stone footings and two long horizontal glass vanes; no face, bodybuilder torso or angel wings.
bosses.materials: Clear thick optical crystal, mineral inclusions, worn dark stone joints.

story.role: Provides a specific institutional conflict with a concrete repair, without making every Arcanean authority secretly malevolent.

bosses.name: Draeven
bosses.title: The Chain Admiral
bosses.summary: A naval aggressor who uses chains, tide and labour schedules with the same deliberate violence.
bosses.faction: Void Ascendants, Blackwake occupation fleet.
bosses.ecology: Depends on pressed shipwrights, tide tables and sound hulls. His grapnels redirect existing loads; he cannot conjure infinite chains or command the harbour animal.
bosses.history: Draeven occupied a refuge harbour to build a blockade that will isolate the frontier. He punishes sabotage by sounding feeding alarms near escape boats, a cruelty his own work crews have learned to document and exploit.
bosses.rivalry: The Keelbreaker destroys hulls when launch work grows loud. Draeven uses that danger against captives but cannot keep the predator away from his flagship’s resonant keel.
bosses.movement: Wide braced stances support two different grapnel lines. A slack chain signals a swing; a fully tensioned line signals a pull that changes the arena load.
bosses.entrance: A capstan stops turning, though the men pushing it do not. At the far end of the chain, the admiral tightens one gloved hand and asks which shipwright cut the brake.

encounter.objective: Break the launch timetable, free the pressed crews and defeat or capture the occupying commander.
encounter.arena: A wet launch deck around a suspended keel, three capstans, two evacuation gantries and tidal sea gates.

phases.name: Two anchors
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches the launch deck.
phases.action: One grapnel sweeps low while the other anchors a pull; chain tension reveals which attack is active.
phases.counterplay: Step over the slack low sweep, stay clear of the taut line and close on the hand committed to the capstan.

phases.name: Load released
phases.trigger: A launch brake is sabotaged or the first capstan is seized.
phases.action: He releases a suspended brace to split the deck, then swings to the surviving gantry.
phases.counterplay: Watch the brake pin and load shadow, secure the evacuation side first and follow only after the brace stops moving.

phases.name: No fleet to command
phases.trigger: The premature launch blocks the fleet channel.
phases.action: He attempts to seize an evacuation boat with both grapnels, abandoning his stable stance.
phases.counterplay: Cut or unhook the exposed lines, use the tide to pull him off the boat route and resolve the final close fight on the pinned gangway.

encounter.failure: A completed launch establishes the blockade and strands part of the frontier convoy. The campaign continues through a harder land route rather than resetting the fleet.
encounter.aftermath: Freed crews retain the arsenal and testify to the occupation. Seized orders identify the exterior bridge interdiction as the second half of the same campaign.

bosses.anatomy: Tall heavily built middle-aged human man with close-cut dark beard, storm-black long coat, salt-white sash, one long chain with a grapnel in each gloved hand, practical weathered shoulder protection.
bosses.materials: Wet wool, blackened steel chain, rough leather and sea salt.

story.role: The first trilogy’s strategic antagonist, whose defeat depends on choices made at the furnace and citadel.

bosses.name: The Keelbreaker
bosses.title: Hunger Beneath the Arsenal
bosses.summary: A flat-armoured harbour predator that discovers ships by the sounds their builders cannot avoid making.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated marine crustacean.
bosses.ecology: Locates prey and hollow shelter through low waterborne vibration. Its broad claw lifts and crushes; its smaller claw blocks openings and handles prey. It cannot pursue a party up a dry cliff.
bosses.history: The animal used tidal caves before the arsenal expanded. Heavy pile-driving and suspended hollow hulls now concentrate its feeding attempts beneath occupied docks.
bosses.rivalry: Draeven’s alarm system repeatedly lures it into the launch basin. It threatens his fleet more than his own fighters because the flagship’s keel produces the strongest resonance.
bosses.movement: Low lateral scuttles fit beneath keels. Before a major lift, six legs spread and the broad claw seats beneath the load, creating an unmistakable commitment.
bosses.entrance: A ship keel rises against its hanging chains. Beneath it, a claw larger than the launch gate closes slowly around the timber.

encounter.objective: Open an unoccupied tidal exit and remove the feeding alarm, or defeat the predator without collapsing the evacuation gantries.
encounter.arena: A flooded dock beneath the launch deck, with stone caissons, hanging hulls and two tide-controlled exits.

phases.name: Hollow timber
phases.trigger: Hammering or an alarm vibrates through a hull.
phases.action: It seats the broad claw beneath the resonant load, then lifts while the small claw blocks the nearest ladder.
phases.counterplay: Leave the load’s vertical shadow, use the stone caisson ladder and disable the alarm during the wide-leg lift.

phases.name: Dock trapped
phases.trigger: The first sea gate is opened.
phases.action: The tide turns it sideways and it sweeps the smaller claw across the lower catwalk.
phases.counterplay: Read the current through floating debris, climb above the sweep and clear the second gate’s jam from the dry mechanism.

phases.name: Open tide
phases.trigger: Both the quiet exit and the alarm shutdown are complete.
phases.action: It follows the current into the outer cave, stopping when a hollow hull vibrates behind it.
phases.counterplay: Keep evacuation work quiet until the shell clears; secure loose timbers before restarting capstans.

encounter.failure: A falling keel destroys a gantry and closes one evacuation lane. Continued alarm use drives the animal back into the inhabited basin.
encounter.aftermath: The harbour resumes with quiet work intervals and a protected outer tide route. The predator remains a serious operational hazard rather than a domesticated trophy.

bosses.anatomy: Massive low flat marine crustacean with two unequal broad crushing claws, six walking legs, tiny protected stalk eyes and a thick ridged shell shaped to wedge beneath hulls; no smiling crab face.
bosses.materials: Dark blue-black weathered shell, pale scrape marks, barnacles, streaming water.

story.role: Makes the liberation plan respect a nonhuman danger that military victory alone cannot remove.

bosses.name: The Ashen Astronomer
bosses.title: Witness of the Eclipsed Meridian
bosses.summary: A scholar willing to make public survival depend on his private observation. His weapon is precise, portable and constrained by the sky.
bosses.faction: Independent claimant of the Ash Meridian observation; proposed Gate-Touched mortal.
bosses.ecology: Needs an aligned crescent instrument, clear sight marks and the short eclipse window. His cloth blindfold filters painful glare rather than granting universal sight.
bosses.history: Years of failed funding and stolen credit hardened into a plan to sell the only accurate water-route measurement. His deliberate coercion is a proposed independent mortal wrongdoing and therefore EXPERIMENTAL under the present antagonist rule.
bosses.rivalry: Veyrath’s migration both reveals the lens well he needs and shifts the causeway holding his instrument. He cannot secure the observation by simply killing the animal without burying the well again.
bosses.movement: Shuffles along inscribed sight marks with the crescent braced on one shoulder. A long tilt precedes a narrow cutting reflection; lowering the instrument leaves a vulnerable but faster human fighter.
bosses.entrance: The desert darkens at midday. On a thin causeway, the scholar lifts a bronze crescent and a white line appears across every approach except his own.

encounter.objective: Secure an independently usable water-route observation and stop the scholar coercing the waiting caravans.
encounter.arena: A central sighting ring, two lower observation stations and a buried lens well exposed during the migration.

phases.name: Claim of sight
phases.trigger: The challenger enters the ring before totality.
phases.action: He tilts the crescent through a broad reflection until a narrow line fixes along one causeway.
phases.counterplay: Leave the brightening line during the slow tilt and approach along a station outside its fixed sight marks.

phases.name: Moving ground
phases.trigger: Veyrath passes beneath the outer ring.
phases.action: He abandons a shifting mark and throws sand to conceal his next instrument brace.
phases.counterplay: Read the instrument’s silhouette against the corona, use the stable lower station and preserve the second observer’s line of sight.

phases.name: Shared sky
phases.trigger: The two lower stations establish an independent measurement.
phases.action: He must choose between finishing his observation and attacking the observers with ordinary close weapon work.
phases.counterplay: Protect the observer during the final count, then disarm, capture or force him to yield the central record.

encounter.failure: A missed measurement increases route uncertainty and water cost. Killing the scholar too early can destroy the only correctly aligned central reading without cancelling the need to save the caravans.
encounter.aftermath: Two independent records prevent monopoly. The scholar can survive to dispute credit or face custody; his knowledge remains useful without excusing his coercion.

bosses.anatomy: Emaciated tall human scholar with mature dark face, blindfold of thin pale cloth, long rust-red weathered mantle and a large portable crescent instrument supported against one shoulder; no floating astrology symbols.
bosses.materials: Sand-worn bronze, dry linen, dark skin, chalk sight marks.

story.role: Gives Corvin and Fenwick a conflict where the answer is public verifiability rather than a stronger spell.

bosses.name: Veyrath
bosses.title: The Dune Cathedral
bosses.summary: A migrating desert mollusc whose shell moves the horizon and whose path exposes the water beneath it.
bosses.faction: Unaffiliated desert fauna.
bosses.ecology: Follows buried brine and scrapes mineral films with a low feeding slit. A broad muscular foot distributes weight over sand; shell sails shade moisture-retaining channels rather than functioning as ornamental towers.
bosses.history: Repeated shell scars correspond to observatory rings from earlier desert routes. Caravan lore describes several such organisms; Veyrath is the expedition’s label for this individual, not a primordial singularity.
bosses.rivalry: The Astronomer’s buried lens covers a brine channel in its path. He needs its passage to uncover that lens but attempts to hurry it with vibrations that threaten his own causeway.
bosses.movement: Slow lateral gliding produces huge pressure changes at the edges of the foot. Shell ribs shed sand before the next turn, and a contracting lower mantle announces a defensive surge.
bosses.entrance: Three apparent ridgelines move against the eclipse. Sand pours from their edges until the low dark foot becomes visible beneath them.

encounter.objective: Cross the moving ring and reach the revealed lens well without forcing the animal into the waiting caravans.
encounter.arena: A partly buried observation ring beside a broad migration channel, with shell-side ledges and two stable salt outcrops.

phases.name: Passing mass
phases.trigger: The animal meets the buried observatory ring.
phases.action: Its foot lifts the outer causeway and sand pours from the leading shell ribs.
phases.counterplay: Move towards a stable outcrop, avoid the compressed sand edge and cross a shell-side ledge only after its load settles.

phases.name: Defensive surge
phases.trigger: Artificial vibration or repeated attacks strike the shell.
phases.action: The lower mantle contracts, then the body shifts laterally across the nearest trench.
phases.counterplay: Read the mantle contraction, leave the trench and silence the vibration source before a second surge.

phases.name: Exposed well
phases.trigger: The rear shell clears the ring.
phases.action: Sand drains into a wake channel and the lens well opens briefly before settling.
phases.counterplay: Anchor a line from the salt outcrop, descend outside the drain funnel and secure the well lip before the next sand fall.

encounter.failure: A forced diversion sends pressure towards the caravan basin and buries a lower observation station. Killing the animal leaves an immense carcass obstructing the water route.
encounter.aftermath: The completed chart includes a seasonal migration interval and an accessible lens well. Wonder survives the encounter because the organism continues beyond the human plot.

bosses.anatomy: Enormous desert mollusc with a long low muscular foot and an asymmetrical ribbed shell rising like three joined wind-eroded sails, narrow feeding slit, no eyes or dragon head.
bosses.materials: Chalky shell, dry orange grit, dark leathery foot, mineral scars.

story.role: Changes the expedition’s map through a living event rather than a convenient treasure-room reveal.

bosses.name: The Sable Testament
bosses.title: Voice of the Outer Wound
bosses.summary: An exterior siege construction whose hanging stone weights translate tension into the destruction of a frontier bridge.
bosses.faction: Void Ascendants, outer-road interdiction working.
bosses.ecology: A bounded root-fibre apparatus powered through existing Shadow-tainted components. Its effect follows six physical anchor lines within the ravine; it has no remote access to Malachar’s prison.
bosses.history: The working was assembled from local roots and prepared basalt weights to complete the blockade campaign by land. Its title is an operator’s theatrical designation, not a sacred text or new cosmic speaker.
bosses.rivalry: Mordren protects the lines but must cross them to reach intruders. His reflection feint is disrupted whenever a weight drops silt into the water, briefly making their tactics interfere.
bosses.movement: The suspended knot tightens before lifting a weight. Only the causeway section connected to that line fractures; inactive lines remain slack and readable.
bosses.entrance: One basalt weight rises out of black water. Far above it, a matching section of the causeway breaks while the hanging root knot turns without a face.

encounter.objective: Stop the local bridge-destruction sequence, secure the convoy and preserve an alternate crossing.
encounter.arena: The exterior ravine only: six weighted lines, three surviving causeway sections, two anchor platforms and an identified downstream ford.

phases.name: Tension named
phases.trigger: The convoy enters the exterior road approach.
phases.action: One line pulls taut, its weight rises and the matching causeway joint sheds stone before fracturing.
phases.counterplay: Trace the visible line, clear that section and pin the active weight from its remote anchor platform.

phases.name: Paired loads
phases.trigger: Two weights are pinned or unloaded.
phases.action: The knot alternates between two remaining lines, forcing a choice of crossing and repair order.
phases.counterplay: Use the previously pinned line as a stable route, unload the heavier visible weight first and move the convoy only after the second line goes slack.

phases.name: Working isolated
phases.trigger: All six lines are unloaded or severed at their local anchors.
phases.action: The central knot contracts into a short final pull confined to its own supports.
phases.counterplay: Withdraw from those supports, secure the last convoy line and contain the inert Shadow-tainted components without approaching the distant fissure.

encounter.failure: A lost causeway section increases evacuation time and may cost wagons. The failure state concerns the local convoy and road; Malachar’s sealed condition never changes.
encounter.aftermath: Stopping the apparatus exposes the downstream ford and preserves evidence of the land blockade. The prison remains sealed and outside the encounter.

bosses.anatomy: A huge suspended mass of tightly woven black root fibres shaped into a long vertical knot with six heavy hanging stone seals; no humanoid head, tentacles or winged demon silhouette.
bosses.materials: Wet black root fibre, rough basalt seal weights, a thin deep red inner light.

story.role: The material climax of the evidence trilogy, linking recovered records to an immediate rescue without escalating into a canon-breaking cosmic release.

bosses.name: Mordren
bosses.title: The Last Duskblade
bosses.summary: A swordmaster whose delayed draw and water reflection make one restrained blade feel impossibly early.
bosses.faction: Voidtouched duelist attached to the exterior Void Ascendant operation.
bosses.ecology: The reflection feint requires a calm connected surface of water within the ravine. Disturbed or obscured water breaks its visual alignment; the real blade remains the source of physical injury.
bosses.history: Mordren accepted Shadow corruption to win duels he could otherwise lose, then committed himself to the blockade’s exterior operation. This proposal does not establish a new primordial, replace Malachar or extend the sealed antagonist’s reach.
bosses.rivalry: The Sable Testament’s falling weights disturb the reflective water and interrupt his best feint. He protects its anchors despite that disadvantage because completing the interdiction matters more to him than a beautiful duel.
bosses.movement: A narrow side-on stance conceals the draw length. The stone scabbard turns before each committed cut; half-draws can become short thrusts but cannot instantly become full sweeps without another shoulder rotation.
bosses.entrance: A plain blade is drawn halfway above the severed causeway. In the water below, its reflection appears fully extended before the hand moves again.

encounter.objective: Break the duelist’s defence of the outer anchors and keep the convoy crossing open.
encounter.arena: A severed causeway over calm black water, two low silt-release sluices and three dry stone islands within the exterior route.

phases.name: Half a blade
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches the first defended anchor.
phases.action: A half-draw threatens a thrust while the reflected image suggests a wider cut.
phases.counterplay: Track the real scabbard and shoulder, hold outside thrust range and punish the full draw’s committed recovery.

phases.name: Water broken
phases.trigger: A siege weight falls or a silt sluice opens.
phases.action: The reflection feint fails; Mordren shifts to fast direct combinations and a scabbard check.
phases.counterplay: Keep the water disturbed, read the three-beat footwork and counter after the scabbard hand crosses his body.

phases.name: Anchor abandoned
phases.trigger: The last convoy line reaches safety or the working is isolated.
phases.action: He leaves the anchor to pursue the bearer of the recovered operation record.
phases.counterplay: Choose the dry island for the final duel, protect the record carrier and defeat, capture or force him off the exterior road.

encounter.failure: An exposed record carrier can be wounded and the operation evidence lost while the convoy still survives. Pursuit never opens a route to the canonical prison.
encounter.aftermath: His defeat ends this exterior protection detail. Surviving corruption is contained locally; no final line claims Shadow itself has ended.

bosses.anatomy: Adult androgynous human swordmaster with severe weathered face and close-cropped white hair, plain black layered warcloth, one unadorned long narrow blade and a broken dark stone scabbard, visible Shadow veins restrained to left hand.
bosses.materials: Matte warcloth, worn steel, black stone, human skin and restrained Shadow absorption.

story.role: A dangerous chosen enemy whose tactical commitment gives the final duel a specific purpose beyond spectacle.
